Section(s): 2.1. Detailed Langmuir-Hinshelwood kinetic model

Text and equations in reading order:
    Using the quasi equilibrium assumption (QEA) for the fast reactions, one can calculate the reaction rates for the CO-hydrogenation, $ CO_{2} $-hydrogenation and the reverse-water-gas shift reaction as follows
(4) r_{\mathrm{{C O}}}=k_{1}\left(p_{\mathrm{{C O}}}p_{\mathrm{{H}_{2}}}^{2}-\frac{p_{\mathrm{{C H}_{3}\mathrm{{O H}}}}}{K_{\mathrm{{P}1}}}\right)\Theta^{\odot}\Theta^{\otimes}    [code: algebraic, computes r_{CO}, code proposes constitutive]
    Here partial pressures are used instead of fugacities, which is justified by the fact that fugacity coefficients are close to one for the operating conditions considered in this paper (Vollbrecht, 2007). The corresponding surface coverages are given by
(7) \Theta^{\odot}=\left(1+\underbrace{K_{\mathrm{CO}}}_{\beta_{8}}p_{\mathrm{CO}}+\underbrace{\left(K_{\mathrm{A3}}K_{\mathrm{CO}}K_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}^{3/2}\right)}_{\beta_{9}}p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}^{3/2}p_{\mathrm{CO}}+\underbrace{K_{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{OH}}^{\odot}}_{\beta_{10}}p_{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{OH}}+\underbrace{K_{\mathrm{CO}_{2}}}_{\beta_{11}}p_{\mathrm{CO}_{2}}\right)^{-}    [code: algebraic, computes \Theta^{\odot}, code proposes constitutive]
(8) \Theta^{\otimes}=\left(1+\underbrace{\sqrt{K_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}}_{ \beta_{7}}\sqrt{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}\right)^{-1}    [code: algebraic, computes \Theta^{\otimes}, code proposes constitutive]
(9) \boldsymbol{\Theta}^{*}=\left(1+\underbrace{\frac{K_{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}}{K_{\mathrm{B}8}K_{\mathrm{B}9}K_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}_{\beta_{13}}\frac{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}}{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}+\underbrace{\frac{K_{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{OH}}^{*}}{K_{\mathrm{B}5}K_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}^{1/2}}}_{\beta_{16}}\frac{p_{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{OH}}}{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}^{1/2}+\underbrace{K_{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{OH}}^{*}}_{\beta_{14}}p_{\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{OH}}++\underbrace{\frac{K_{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}}{K_{\mathrm{B}9}K_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}^{1/2}}}_{\beta_{15}}\frac{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}}{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}^{1/2}+\underbrace{K_{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}}_{\beta_{12}}p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}\right)^{-}    [code: algebraic, computes \Theta^{*}, code proposes constitutive]
    Therein, a reparametrization is introduced as indicated with the lumped $ \beta_{i} $ parameters, which have to be fitted to experimental data. A known problem for the parameter estimation is the correlation between frequency factor and activation energy, which impedes reasonable results. Therefore, the following reformulation of the Arrhenius-equation is used (Schwaab et al., 2008; Schwaab and Pinto, 2007; Xu and Froment, 1989):
(10) k_{i}=\exp\left(\underbrace{A}_{\beta_{1},\beta_{3},\beta_{5}}-\underbrace{B}_{\beta_{2},\beta_{4},\beta_{6}}\left(\frac{T_{ref}}{T}-1\right)\right)    [code: algebraic, computes k_{i}, code proposes constitutive]
    with reference temperature $ T_{ref} = 523.15\ K $ and equilibrium constants according to Vollbrecht (2007).

Symbols:
  r_{CO}: Rate of CO hydrogenation. (computed)
  k_{1}: Kinetic rate constant for CO hydrogenation. (parameter)
  p_{CO}: Partial pressure of CO. (variable)
  p_{H_2}: Partial pressure of hydrogen. (variable)
  p_{CH_3OH}: Partial pressure of methanol. (variable)
  K_{P1}: Equilibrium constant for the CO-hydrogenation reaction. (computed)
  \Theta^{\odot}: Surface coverage on ⊙ sites. [-] (computed)
  \Theta^{\otimes}: Surface coverage on ⊗ sites. [-] (computed)
  K_{CO}: Equilibrium constant for CO adsorption on ⊙ sites. (parameter)
  K_{A3}: Equilibrium constant in the composite hydrogen–CO adsorption term of the ⊙-site coverage expression. (parameter)
  K_{H_2}: Equilibrium constant for hydrogen adsorption on vacant ⊗ sites. [bar^-1] (parameter)
  K_{CH_3OH}^{\odot}: Adsorption equilibrium constant for methanol on ⊙ sites. [bar^-1] (parameter)
  K_{CO_2}: Equilibrium constant for CO₂ adsorption on ⊙ sites. [bar^-1] (parameter)
  p_{CO_2}: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide used in the model equations. [bar] (variable)
  \Theta^{*}: Free reduced surface centers relative to the total amount of reduced surface centers. [-] (computed)
  K_{H_2O}: Equilibrium constant for H₂O adsorption on reduced surface centers. [bar^-1] (parameter)
  K_{B8}: Equilibrium constant for the H⊗ + O* ⇌ OH* + ⊗ surface step. [-] (parameter)
  K_{B9}: Equilibrium constant for the H⊗ + OH* ⇌ H₂O* + ⊗ surface step. [-] (parameter)
  \beta_{13}: Model-specific fitted coefficient in a surface-coverage expression. [model-dependent] (parameter)
  p_{H_2O}: Partial pressure of water used in the model equations. [bar] (variable)
  K_{CH_3OH}^{*}: Methanol adsorption equilibrium constant in the surface-coverage equation. [bar^-1] (parameter)
  K_{B5}: Quasi-equilibrium constant in the relation for elementary step B5. [-] (parameter)
  k_{i}: Rate constant. (computed)
  A: Arrhenius exponent parameter in the reformulated rate-constant equation. [-] (parameter)
  B: Temperature-dependence parameter in the reformulated Arrhenius equation. [-] (parameter)
  T_{ref}: Reference temperature. [K] (parameter)
  T: Temperature. [K] (variable)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Catalyst deactivation neglected; only reactions (1)-(3) considered.
  - Langmuir‑Hinshelwood mechanism with adsorption, surface reaction, desorption.
  - Oxidized centers (⊙) are active for CO hydrogenation.
  - Reduced centers (∗) are active for CO₂ hydrogenation.
  - Total numbers of oxidized, reduced and hydrogen centers are constant.
  - Fast steps are at quasi‑equilibrium.
  - Quasi‑equilibrium assumption for fast adsorption/desorption steps.
  - Lumped kinetics for reactions (1)-(3).
  - Two alternatives for φ: quasistatic (Eq.22) or dynamic (Eq.28).
